title: Obligation and advice
grammar: Must, Have to, Should, Must not, Do not have to

sections.heading: Modal verbs for obligation and advice
sections.body: Modal verbs express obligation, prohibition and advice. They do not change form and are followed by the base verb.

sections.heading: Must / Mustn't
sections.body: 'Must' expresses strong obligation (often personal). 'Mustn't' means prohibition.

sections.heading: Have to / Don't have to
sections.body: 'Have to' expresses external obligation (rules from outside). 'Don't have to' means no obligation.
table: I have to work on Saturdays.

sections.heading: Should / Shouldn't
list: You should see a doctor.
You should drink more water.
You shouldn't eat too much sugar.
You shouldn't work so hard.

sections.heading: Must vs Have to
table: I have to wear a uniform.

sections.heading: Common mistakes
list: Do not use 'to' after modals: 'You must to go' is wrong.
Do not add -s to modals: 'She musts' is wrong.
Do not confuse 'mustn't' (forbidden) with 'don't have to' (not necessary).

list.definition: You have to queue in Britain.
You should rest if you are tired.
You should sleep 8 hours a night.
You have to follow the rules.
You have to work in a team.

phases.name: Discovery
phases.intro: Look at these sentences. Read them carefully and think about the questions below.
sentences: You must wear a seatbelt in the car.
You mustn't smoke in the hospital.
You shouldn't eat too much sugar.
I have to work on Saturdays.
She has to wear a uniform at school.
You don't have to come. It's optional.
We don't have to pay for children under 5.
questions: In sentences 1 and 2, what is the difference between 'must' and 'mustn't'?
In sentences 3 and 4, what is 'should' used for?
In sentences 5 and 6, what is 'have to' used for?
In sentences 7 and 8, what does 'don't have to' mean?
In all sentences, do the modal verbs change form with he/she/it?

questions.prompt: You ___ smoke in the hospital. It is forbidden.
You ___ see a doctor. You look ill.
I ___ wear a seatbelt. It's the law.
You ___ come if you don't want to.
questions.explanation: Don't have to means no obligation.

questions.prompt: She ___ work on Sundays.
You ___ eat so much sugar. It's bad for you.
We ___ pay. The entrance is free.
Students ___ arrive on time.
You ___ use your phone during the exam.
I ___ study more for the test.

phases.name: Free practice
prompts: Write 5 pieces of advice for someone who wants to learn English. Use 'should' and 'shouldn't'.
Write 5 rules for your classroom or workplace using 'must', 'mustn't' and 'have to'.
Write 5 things you have to do this week and 5 things you don't have to do.

questions.prompt: You ___ drink more water in summer.
Passengers ___ wear a seatbelt.
You ___ come to the meeting if you are busy.
She ___ study harder.
We ___ be quiet in the library.
You ___ use your phone at the table.
I ___ work on Saturday. It's my day off.
He ___ wear a suit for work.
You ___ eat so much fast food.
Visitors ___ sign in at reception.

sections.heading: Key rules
list: Must: strong personal obligation. Mustn't: prohibition.
Have to: external obligation. Don't have to: no obligation.
Should: advice. Shouldn't: negative advice.
Modal verbs do not change form and are followed by the base verb.

sections.heading: Common mistakes
list: Do not use 'to' after a modal: 'You must to go' is wrong.
Do not add -s to modals: 'She musts' is wrong.
Do not confuse 'mustn't' (forbidden) with 'don't have to' (not necessary).

sections.heading: Useful phrases
list: You must...
You mustn't...
You have to...
You don't have to...
You should...
You shouldn't...
